record.original_question: Find necessary and sufficient conditions on a general class of positive integer sequences so that, for a fixed n, there exist n distinct sequences from that class whose union covers all positive integers. In particular, for recurrence-defined classes Af = {(a_n) : a_n = f(a_{n-1},...,a_{n-i}) for n > i+1 with positive integer initial data}, determine when such covering is possible under the surjectivity-type conditions stated in the source.

evidence.quote: *Find a necessary and sufficient condition for a general class of positive integer sequences such that, for a fixed n, there are n (distinct) sequences of this class which cover all integers.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a class of strictly increasing (or just non-repeating) sequences of positive integers. Say that sequences $S_1,\dots,S_n\in\mathcal{C}$ cover the positive integers if every positive integer belongs to at least one $S_k$, viewed as a set of values.

(a) Find necessary and sufficient conditions on the class $\mathcal{C}$ such that, for a given fixed integer $n\ge 1$, there exist $n$ distinct sequences $S_1,\dots,S_n\in\mathcal{C}$ whose union of value sets equals $\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$.

(b) Specialize to the following recurrence-defined classes. For a positive integer $i$ and a function $f:\mathbb{Z}_{>0}^{i}\to\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, let
$$\mathcal{A}_f \;=\;\bigl\{(a_n)_{n\ge 1}\subset\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\;:\; a_n=f(a_{n-1},a_{n-2},\dots,a_{n-i})\text{ for all }n>i\bigr\},$$
where the initial tuple $(a_1,\dots,a_i)\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}^{i}$ ranges over all positive integer initial data. Assume $f$ satisfies a surjectivity-type condition (e.g. that the induced map on initial tuples gives every eventual value achievable). Determine, for which $f$ and which $n$, there exist $n$ distinct sequences in $\mathcal{A}_f$ that together cover every positive integer.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted search did not locate a published resolution of the general criterion for when n distinct sequences from a class (in particular a recurrence-defined class $\mathcal{A}_f$) cover the positive integers. Related literature on completeness of positive linear recurrence sequences (Brown's criterion and its descendants) addresses representability by sums rather than set-theoretic covering by n sequences, so the status of the stated problem appears unresolved in the available sources.

status_evidence.title: An Introduction to Completeness of Positive Linear Recurrence Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of completeness (sum representability) of positive linear recurrence sequences; discusses Brown's criterion and necessary/sufficient conditions, but for sum-coverings, not set-coverings by n sequences.
status_evidence.claim: The closely related completeness problem concerns sums of distinct terms, not n-fold set covers, so it does not resolve the stated question.

status_evidence.title: Completeness of Positive Linear Recurrence Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Studies when positive linear recurrence sequences are complete in the sum sense; does not address covering positive integers by n distinct sequences drawn from a recurrence-defined class.
status_evidence.claim: No general necessary and sufficient condition for n-sequence set covers from a class $\mathcal{A}_f$ is established.
